name: Tweek
tagline: A minimal weekly calendar and to-do planner laid out as seven columns you can drag tasks between.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Tweek is a weekly grid with draggable text rows, and that is genuinely the whole product. There is no proprietary data, no network, no model, just a tidy layout and pleasant drag behavior. An agent can produce a local version with recurring tasks, colors, keyboard entry and a SQLite or JSON store in one sitting. What you will not get for free is the polished mobile app, Google Calendar sync, and shared lists with a partner. If you plan alone on a laptop, the DIY version is fine and arguably faster because it opens instantly.
coreLoopDIY: A seven-column week view where you type tasks into days, drag them between days, check them off, and roll unfinished ones forward, stored locally.
requirements: Local SQLite or a JSON file for storage
Optional: a Google Calendar API key if you want read-only event overlay
whatYouLose: Native iOS and Android apps with offline sync
Two-way Google Calendar and Todoist style integrations
Shared weeks and collaborative lists with someone else
Cross-device sync without you running a server
The specific fit and finish of the drag interactions
moatNotes: The moat is taste and mobile builds, not technology. Copying the layout is trivial; copying the feel of it on a phone is the actual work.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for Tweek because planning tools only work if they are open on the device you actually have, which usually means a phone. A local web app you built yourself dies the moment you are standing in a queue and want to add something. The subscription is really renting a synced mobile client and someone else's decisions about spacing and animation, which is a reasonable thing to rent if you do not want to maintain a personal server for a to-do list.
notes: One of those rare apps where the DIY version is genuinely competitive, provided you never leave your desk.
prompt:
Build a local weekly planner web app in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- dnd-kit for drag and drop
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 behind a tiny Express API in the same repo
- Single user, no auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud

Core UI:
- A seven column grid, Monday through Sunday, each column a day of the current week
- Header shows the week range with prev / next / today buttons
- Clicking empty space in a day creates an inline text input; Enter saves and opens the next blank row, Escape cancels
- Tasks are single line text with an optional color label chosen from a fixed palette of six
- Click a task to edit in place, click the checkbox to complete (strikethrough, dimmed, stays in place)
- Drag tasks within a day to reorder and across days to reschedule, using dnd-kit
- An extra "Someday" column pinned to the right, not tied to a date

Behaviors:
- Recurring tasks: daily, weekly on the same weekday, or every N weeks. Store the rule, generate occurrences for the viewed week on the fly, completing one occurrence does not affect others
- "Roll over" button that moves all unfinished tasks from past days into today
- Keyboard: arrow keys move focus between tasks, cmd+enter toggles complete
- Full text search across all tasks with results grouped by week

Data:
- Tables: tasks (id, text, day date nullable, sort order, color, done at, recurrence rule id nullable), recurrences, completions
- Export and import the whole database as JSON from a settings panel

Out of scope: mobile apps, calendar sync, sharing, notifications, dark mode toggle beyond respecting prefers-color-scheme.

Secrets, if any are ever added, go in .env with a committed .env.example. Ship a README with one command to run both API and frontend, and seed data for the current week so the grid is not empty on first launch.
